sources.finding: Official municipal heritage locates decision to construct internal citadel under governor Edward Poynings in 1515; separates northern walled sector; local municipal and military friction; identifies Pont des Trous and internal gate design.
Heritage entry says English urban rule 1513–1519, tower survived; internal citadel expected large garrison; geography of walls in northern part.

Says English troops departed in 1519 and city was bought back by Francis I; also inaccurately says Tournai had Westminster MPs, contradicted by C.S.L. Davies 1998; do not rely for parliamentary claim.
Peer reviewed source supports town council's negotiated local privileges and February 1519 practical return; English imposition not identical to Calais territorial incorporation.
Academic paper says no representation in English Parliament and legal title was Henry VIII's French kingdom, not England proper.

issues.claim: Tournai English citadel built in 1513 immediately after town captured
issues.best_evidence: Municipality identifies decision for internal castle in 1515; Murphy article discusses Tournai workers April–Oct 1517 and garrison occupation January 1518. 1513 official tourism may summarize occupation beginning as construction date. 1513 = capture, 1515/17/18 = fort process.
issues.impact: Do not put citadel-complete icon at 1513; historical English tower survives today but not an instant 1513 building.

issues.claim: Henry VIII let Tournai send MPs to the House of Commons (official visitor webpage)
issues.resolution: academically disputed / incorrect according to expert reassessment
issues.best_evidence: C.S.L. Davies 1998 peer-reviewed study specifically states Tournai was NOT granted representation in the English Parliament; tourist page asserts MPs without primary citation.
issues.impact: Use Davies claim pending original Commons returns; do not repeat tourist anecdote as fact.

issues.claim: Tourist brochure says English rule 1513–1518; local military museum says six years; scholarly sources 1513–1519.
issues.resolution: distinguish legal cession 1518 from actual occupation to Feb 1519
issues.best_evidence: British Library Add MS48002 4 Oct 1518 cession treaty; Murphy scholarly paper details English garrison until February 1519; tourist VisitTournai explicitly says troops left 1519.
issues.impact: 1518 treaty transition event but retain Tournai English-control until Feb 1519; 1519 snapshot after February show French.

issues.claim: City pages disagree on which Scheldt river bank held Henry VIII citadel
issues.resolution: uncertain mapping nomenclature / requires historical-geographic verification
issues.best_evidence: Municipal French description 'rive droite de l'Escaut'; Wallonia heritage text says 'protéger la rive gauche'. Direction may distinguish bank of structure vs bank being protected. Detailed gate/topography could resolve.
issues.impact: Place tower via separately validated address Place Verte, no precise digitized citadel polygon yet.

issues.claim: 1518 600,000 crowns 'profit made' by English Crown from Tournai
issues.best_evidence: Polydore Vergil contemporary later narrative details Francis I to pay 600k crowns over 12 years at 50k per annum, a bargain price term; later arrears and net expenses unknown.
issues.impact: Use monetary_type=promised_cession_consideration; do not totalize as realised extracted colonial net income; verify BL Add MS48002 treaty.

editorial_note: Do not assume municipal tourist information on MPs and 1513 citadel construction is correct when contemporary archival/paper data conflict.
